summary: Brazil admits citizens of the EU, the UK and most of Latin America visa-free for up to 90 days, requires an eVisa (USD 80.90) from US, Canadian and Australian citizens, admits a few others, among them China, visa-free for 30 or 60 days, and asks the remaining nationalities to apply for a visit visa at a Brazilian consulate.

name.text: The Visitor Visa may be granted to visitors who are willing to come to Brazil for a stay of up to 90 days for activities such as tourism and business meetings.

method.text: This section deals with the general requirements for a regular Visitor Visa, which can be obtained in person at the Consulate-General of Brazil in Miami and which is available for citizens of different nationalities, including U.S. citizens.

fee.notes: The Visitor Visa covers stays of up to 90 days for activities such as tourism and business meetings. The Consulate-General of Brazil in Miami sets the fee according to the nationality of the passport you hold; citizens of Australia, Canada and the United States can obtain the electronic visitor visa instead.

passportValidity.text: The eVisa portal says your passport must be valid for at least one more month after your arrival in Brazil, and asks you to check with your airline whether a passport with only one month's validity will be accepted. The Consulate-General of Brazil in Miami tells its visa applicants that their passport must be valid for at least six months after the date they enter Brazil, or, for US passports, until their intended date of return.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Brazil?
faq.answer: Yes. US citizens need an eVisa to visit Brazil. It costs USD 80.90, is applied for online at brazil.vfsevisa.com and is valid for 10 years for US citizens. The eVisa portal says it allows stays of up to 90 days per year and that extensions beyond 90 days are handled by the Federal Police.

faq.question: Which nationalities can visit Brazil without a visa?
faq.answer: Citizens of the EU, the UK, Switzerland, Japan, South Korea, Turkey, South Africa, Mexico and most of South America (among others) can visit visa-free for up to 90 days. US, Canadian and Australian citizens need the eVisa, and nationalities such as Indian and Nigerian citizens need a consular visa.

faq.question: How do I apply for the Brazilian eVisa?
faq.answer: Apply online at the official portal brazil.vfsevisa.com with a colour copy of your passport bio page and a recent photograph, and pay USD 80.90. The portal says processing takes up to 10 business days once your verified application is submitted.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Brazil?
faq.answer: No, it is not an entry requirement: Brazil's Ministry of Health says no proof of vaccination is required to enter the country. It recommends yellow fever vaccination at least 10 days before travel to the areas where vaccination is recommended, and says to carry the International Certificate of Vaccination when a country you travel to or transit through requires it.

faq.question: Can I extend my 90-day stay in Brazil?
faq.answer: Under Decree 9,199/2017 (art. 20), the Federal Police can extend a visit visa's stay by up to 90 days, as long as the total stay does not exceed 180 days in each migratory year. The request must be made before the original stay expires, and extensions are available only to nationals of countries that give Brazilians reciprocal treatment. Article 23 says the same rule may be applied to nationals of visa-exempt countries. The foreign ministry's visa table caps some nationalities, for example Germans and Italians, at 90 days in every 180.
